title: It’s time to really pressure Trump—on Iran, Ukraine and trade
gist: Labour peer Andrew Adonis argues that after Trump's midterm drubbing, western leaders must not disengage but press him hard to reverse three failing policies before 2028: the Iran stand-off (with Iran holding western oil hostage in the Strait of Hormuz), appeasement of Putin over Ukraine, and arbitrary tariffs. He urges Europe to negotiate directly with Iran, deploy frozen Russian assets for Kyiv, and locate a large share of AI data centres within Europe.

themes.theme: Iran stalemate and the Strait of Hormuz

insights.claim: The US-Israeli attempt at regime change in Iran has failed; mass bombing radicalised the regime, which now holds western oil hostage in the Strait of Hormuz.
insights.speaker: Andrew Adonis
insights.so_what: Persistent Hormuz disruption sustains an oil risk premium; energy exposure should price a prolonged stand-off.
insights.quote: The mass bombings instead radicalised the Islamic regime, which now holds western oil hostage in the Strait of Hormuz.
insights.locator: The US-Israeli attempt at regime change

insights.claim: Adonis predicts the Iran stand-off could easily persist another two years as long as Trump refuses to rule out further attacks and demands total Iranian capitulation.
insights.speaker: Andrew Adonis
insights.so_what: Base case of elevated oil prices through 2028 unless US terms soften; watch any Trump shift on ruling out strikes.
insights.quote: This stalemate could easily persist for another two years.
insights.locator: The US-Israeli attempt at regime change

insights.claim: Adonis urges Europe to open direct negotiations with Iran and its neighbours to reopen the Strait of Hormuz, including security and financial arrangements.
insights.speaker: Andrew Adonis
insights.so_what: A European-brokered Hormuz deal would be a catalyst for lower crude and shipping insurance costs.
insights.locator: At the same time as engaging

themes.theme: Ukraine appeasement and frozen Russian assets

insights.claim: Jared Kushner, described as part envoy, part business manager, has been floating 'peace' proposals in which Zelensky would cede territory to Putin for weak security assurances.
insights.speaker: Andrew Adonis
insights.so_what: Risk of a territorial settlement unfavourable to Ukraine; relevant to European defence and reconstruction plays.
insights.locator: The US appeasement of Vladimir Putin

insights.claim: Ukraine's survival over another two years is at risk, particularly if Marine Le Pen, who has pledged to cut aid to Ukraine, becomes president of France next summer.
insights.speaker: Andrew Adonis
insights.so_what: French 2027 presidential election is a key event risk for Ukraine support and EU cohesion.
insights.locator: The US appeasement of Vladimir Putin

insights.claim: Adonis calls for a serious increase in European military and financial aid to Ukraine funded by the billions of pounds of frozen Russian assets in limbo since 2022.
insights.speaker: Andrew Adonis
insights.so_what: Watch for an EU/UK decision on seizing frozen Russian assets — a sovereign-asset and legal-precedent event for custodians and the euro.
insights.locator: At the same time as engaging

themes.theme: Tariffs, China rivalry and European AI sovereignty

insights.claim: Two more years of high, arbitrary and constantly changing US tariffs would be dangerous, especially for Canada and Europe facing intense industrial rivalry with China.
insights.speaker: Andrew Adonis
insights.so_what: Tariff volatility plus Chinese competition weighs on European and Canadian industrials and exporters.

insights.claim: Adonis warns that tariff instability combined with exclusion from US frontier AI products would be worse still for Europe.
insights.speaker: Andrew Adonis
insights.so_what: Access to US frontier AI is a strategic chokepoint; European AI-infrastructure policy could shift sharply.
insights.quote: exclusion from US frontier AI products

insights.claim: Adonis argues Europe cannot gain leverage in the AI revolution unless a large proportion of the data centres powering AI are located within Europe, calling this possibly the biggest policy challenge of all.
insights.speaker: Andrew Adonis
insights.so_what: Supports a policy tailwind for European data-centre build-out, power and grid investment.
insights.quote: a large proportion of the data centres powering AI are located within Europe

insights.claim: Adonis warns that arbitrary US protectionism may not be limited to Trump alone, so Europe should not rely on continued US market access.
insights.speaker: Andrew Adonis
insights.so_what: Treat US protectionism as structural beyond 2028, not a Trump-era anomaly.
insights.quote: arbitrary US protectionism wasn’t limited to Trump alone

themes.theme: Western lobbying strategy after the midterms

insights.claim: Adonis argues it would be a dangerous mistake for Andy Burnham and other western leaders to disengage with relief after the midterms; the worst may be yet to come before the 2028 election.
insights.speaker: Andrew Adonis
insights.so_what: Do not assume midterm losses de-risk US foreign policy; volatility may persist to 2028.
insights.quote: The worst may be yet to come unless US foreign policy changes well before the 2028 presidential election.

insights.claim: Adonis says Burnham, Macron, Merz, Meloni, Carney and Zelensky should lobby Trump, his entourage and new congressional leaders intensively, noting a large part of Washington including parts of the administration agree policy should change.
insights.speaker: Andrew Adonis
insights.so_what: Coordinated western pressure plus a hostile Congress raises odds of a US policy pivot on Iran, Ukraine and trade.
